Other agents call it over A2A; it drives a real coding-agent session in your project — Claude Code, or any agent that speaks Zed's [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com) (ACP): Gemini CLI, Codex, OpenHands, and more — and streams the work back as it happens. L4: [![CI](https://github.com/kanywst/a2acode/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/kanywst/a2acode/actions/workflows/ci.yml) L5: [![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) L6: [![Python 3.13+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.13+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/) L7: [![Protocol: A2A 1.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/protocol-A2A%201.0-D97757.svg)](https://a2aprotocol.ai/) L8: ![a2acode streaming a task, then pausing on a permission prompt](assets/demo.gif) L9: Most adapters that put a coding agent behind A2A flatten everything to text in, text out. a2acode keeps the structure the agent produces: the tools it runs, the files it changes, what it costs, the approvals it needs, and how to continue on the next turn. It bridges two Linux Foundation interop standards — **ACP** (how editors and clients talk to coding agents) on the agent side, **A2A** (how agents delegate to each other) on the caller side — so any ACP agent becomes a peer any A2A orchestrator can call. L10: ## How it maps to A2A L11: | The coding agent produces | A2A surface it lands on | L12: | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | L13: | Assistant text | A streamed artifact (`append` / `last_chunk`) | L14: | Its reasoning | A separate `thinking` artifact, never the answer | L15: | A tool call (Bash, Edit) | A `working` status update for the action | L16: | That tool's outcome | A `working` status update: `✓ Bash` / `✗ Bash: …` | L17: | Its plan for the turn | A `plan` artifact, replaced as steps progress | L18: | A file edit (diff) | A named artifact carrying the diff | L19: | A permission request | An `input-required` pause the caller answers | L20: | Run result | Cost, turns, usage, stop reason on the completion | L21: | Session id | Mapped to the A2A `contextId` so follow-ups resume | L22: The mapping is all in `executor.py`. Backends only emit normalized events; they never touch the protocol. L23: ## Where this fits L24: L25: Anthropic now ships its own ways to run Claude Code beyond the terminal: Claude Code on the web, background agents, cloud-hosted Routines, and the Managed Agents API. These are the right choices when you want Anthropic to host the run and you live in their ecosystem, and they are typically tied to Anthropic infrastructure and a GitHub-centric flow. L26: a2acode solves a different problem: making any coding agent a first-class peer on a vendor-neutral [A2A](https://a2aprotocol.ai/) mesh. An orchestrator built on any framework discovers it through its agent card and delegates coding work the same way it would to any other A2A agent. The run happens on infrastructure you control, in a workspace you point it at. Reach for a2acode when: L27: - another agent (not a human at a prompt) is the caller, and it speaks A2A; L28: - you want the run on your own infrastructure and data boundary, not a vendor VM; L29: - you do not want to bet on one vendor's coding agent: ACP makes the backend a launch-command choice, so swapping Claude Code for Codex, Gemini CLI, or OpenHands does not touch the protocol surface your callers depend on. L30: ACP already standardizes the editor↔agent side and a dozen agents speak it; a2acode is the piece that exposes an ACP agent to *remote autonomous callers* over A2A, with permission round-trips and cost preserved as first-class protocol citizens — the part ACP leaves out because it assumes a human in an editor. The practical user is the platform team building that mesh, not the individual developer. L31: ## Requirements L32: L33: - Python 3.13+ L34: - [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) L35: - An ACP agent adapter for the `acp` backend, launched as a subprocess. Every preset launches one with `npx`, so Node is the only prerequisite besides that agent's own credential: L36: | `--agent` | Launches | Credential | L37: | --------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------- | L38: | `claude` | `@zed-industries/claude-agent-acp` | Anthropic API key | L39: | `codex` | `@zed-industries/codex-acp` | OpenAI credential | L40: | `gemini` | `@google/gemini-cli --acp` | Code Assist Standard or Enterprise | L41: L42: Or point `--agent-command` at any other ACP agent. L43: **On the `gemini` preset:** Google stopped serving the Gemini CLI to consumer accounts on 18 June 2026 — the individual Code Assist tier and AI Pro/Ultra access — and points them at Antigravity instead. A session on one of those fails with *"This client is no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals"*. This is not specific to ACP or to a2acode: it is the whole CLI, on those tiers. Organization Code Assist Standard and Enterprise subscriptions are unaffected, which is why the preset stays. L44: ## Quick start L45: L46: Install: L47: L48: ```bash L49: uv sync L50: ``` L51: L52: The `echo` backend needs no API key and no Claude install, so you can exercise the whole path offline first: L53: L54: ```bash L55: uv run a2acode serve --backend echo & L56: # once the "Uvicorn running" line appears: L57: uv run a2acode call "fix the failing test" L58: ``` L59: L60: ```text L61: task 189b1c63-1a7b-4908-87c4-c8f3bba8f6b5 L62: context 0b2a901e-2b6f-4c56-bba2-d0da546936e9 L63: L64: · Echo L65: fix the failing test L66: [completed] $0.0 · 1 turns L67: ``` L68: Then point it at a real project. The default backend is `acp`, fronting Claude Code through its ACP adapter: L69: L70: ```bash L71: uv run a2acode serve --cwd /path/to/project # acp + claude by default L72: uv run a2acode call "add a /health endpoint" --url http://localhost:9100/ L73: ``` L74: L75: Swap the agent without touching anything else: L76: L77: ```bash L78: uv run a2acode serve --agent gemini --cwd /path/to/project L79: uv run a2acode serve --agent-command "npx -y some-other-acp-agent" L80: ``` L81: Continue the same conversation by passing the `context` from a previous turn: L82: L83: ```bash L84: uv run a2acode call "now add a test for it" --context L85: ``` L86: L87: Continuity needs the agent to support ACP's `session/load`. When it does not, the turn still runs, but on a fresh session — and the task says so in a status update rather than answering as if it remembered. L88: ## Container L89: L90: Every release publishes a `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` image to GHCR, holding the same wheel as the PyPI release with all three extras installed — so which backend and which task store it runs is a flag, not a rebuild. It runs as a non-root user and works in your project by way of whatever you mount over `/workspace`. L91: A container has to listen on every interface to be reachable at all, so the default command binds `0.0.0.0` where the `uv run` quick start binds loopback. That makes *where you publish the port* the boundary: whoever reaches it can run a coding agent in your workspace. Publish it to your own loopback while you try it out — L92: L93: ```bash L94: docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:9100:9100 \ L95: -v "$PWD:/workspace" \ L96: -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY \ L97: ghcr.io/kanywst/a2acode:latest L98: ``` L99: — and on any network wider than that, mount a token file and require it, which also makes the card advertise the scheme: L100: L101: ```bash L102: docker run --rm -p 9100:9100 \ L103: -v "$PWD:/workspace" -v "$PWD/token:/run/token:ro" \ L104: -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY \ L105: ghcr.io/kanywst/a2acode:latest \ L106: serve --host 0.0.0.0 --auth-token-file /run/token L107: ``` L108: See [Caller authentication](#caller-authentication) for what that check covers. As the second example shows, anything you pass replaces the default command, so `--host` has to come with it. L109: L110: `/.well-known/agent-card.json` stays exempt from that check — discovery precedes the credential — which makes it the liveness and readiness probe. There is no separate health endpoint to configure. L111: Two things worth knowing before deploying it. The image carries Node but not any ACP agent adapter, which the `acp` backend fetches with `npx` on the first run: an environment with no npm registry access needs its adapter baked into a layer of your own. And the mounted workspace is written as uid 1000, so pass `--user` if your project's files belong to someone else. L112: ## Commands L113: L114: | Command | Description | L115: | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | L116: | `a2acode serve` | Start the A2A server | L117: | `a2acode call TEXT` | Send a message and print the streamed events | L118: | `a2acode card` | Fetch and print the agent card | L119: The agent card is served at `/.well-known/agent-card.json` and advertises Claude Code's abilities as discrete skills (generation, refactor, debug, review, test, explain). L120: ## Attachments L121: An A2A message is not only text. A caller can attach the failing log, the patch to review, or a screenshot, and the parts reach the agent as content rather than as a note that something was attached: text files are inlined into the prompt, images go to ACP agents that advertise image support as real image blocks, and URL parts arrive as links the agent can fetch. Inlined content is capped per part and per message, and anything trimmed is marked as truncated so the agent knows it is reading a fragment. L122: ## Backends L123: L124: A backend turns a prompt into a stream of normalized events. Three ship today: L125: - `acp` (default): drives any agent that speaks Zed's Agent Client Protocol as a subprocess. `--agent claude|gemini|codex` selects a launch preset; `--agent-command` drives any other ACP agent. This is the vendor-neutral path. The subprocess is kept alive per conversation, so a follow-up turn skips the process launch, the ACP handshake, and the session reload and talks straight to the agent that already holds the conversation. L126: - `claude`: drives Claude Code directly through the Claude Agent SDK, no subprocess. Install with `uv sync --extra claude`. Use it when you want the SDK-native path (e.g. `--max-budget-usd`) rather than ACP. L127: - `echo`: no dependencies, mirrors the input.
